capability.summary: Run the project's default Jest suite with `jest --json` from a supplied project path
capability.description: Uses a directory as the Jest working directory or an existing file's parent, then invokes the PATH-resolved Jest executable with only `--json`. It parses Jest's native JSON result and treats exit codes 0 and 1 as completed test runs.
capability.problem_space: Default JavaScript/TypeScript Jest suite execution with native JSON reporting; not arbitrary npm test execution, Vitest, test-file targeting, coverage collection, snapshot updating, or non-executing result parsing.

env_requirements: jest executable available directly on PATH
project dependencies and Jest configuration required by the test suite
constraint.io_signature: Input: one required existing project directory or file whose parent becomes cwd; output: JSON execution envelope containing parsed Jest native JSON plus exit and stream metadata.
accepted_inputs: an existing JavaScript or TypeScript project directory configured for direct `jest --json` execution
an existing file path whose parent directory should be used as cwd; the file itself is not passed as a Jest test filter
constraint.output_shape: Completed test run (Jest exit 0 or 1): {status: "success", tool: "jest", target: string, exit_code: 0|1, result: object|array|null, stdout: string|null, stderr: string|null}; parsed native JSON from the first valid stdout/stderr stream is stored in result and stdout becomes null. Other Jest exits use the same keys with status="tool_error" and propagate the actual exit code. Non-existing input, missing Jest executable, or 180-second timeout: {status: "error", tool: "jest", message: string}, exiting 2/3/4. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: always runs direct `jest --json` with no test path/pattern, project, config, runInBand, coverage, watch, cache, environment, worker, or passthrough options
a supplied file only selects its parent cwd and is not targeted as the test file
requires a `jest` executable directly on PATH and does not invoke npm, yarn, pnpm, npx, or a package.json script
executes project test code and may use or write Jest caches or trigger test-defined side effects; it uses a fixed 180-second timeout and applies no wrapper truncation

output_contract.description: JSON execution envelope containing parsed native `jest --json` results, target, actual exit code, and remaining stream metadata.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run a project's default Jest test suite
execute Jest and obtain native JSON test results
negative_intents: run Vitest npm test or a generic package script
target one Jest test file or pass custom Jest flags
collect Jest coverage or update snapshots
